Title: Possible Roberts Road Expansion as SpaceX pushes for Flight 16
Author: Ryan Weber
Date: October 25, 2026
Outlet: NASASpaceFlight.com
URL: https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2026/10/roberts-road-expansion-flight-16/

As SpaceX prepares to fly Flight 15 in November, with a successful Static Fire test occurring at Starbase on Sunday, the company is pushing to launch Flight 16 from LC-39A as soon as possible and expand operations at Kennedy Space Center.

To do that, the Gigabay and pad must be ready to host Booster 23 and Ship 43, both of which have completed cryo-proof testing.

Once the deluge system timings and pressures are finalized, LC-39A should be ready to receive vehicles for testing. To that end, Ship 43 recently completed cryo-proof testing on Oct 23 and will soon roll back to Mega Bay 2 for engine install and final assembly.

Ship 43 must be fully finished, including static fire testing, before it can be sent to Roberts Road. This is because SpaceX has no ship-testing capability at Kennedy Space Center, so when it’s sent on the barge, Ship 43 will likely be missing only its payload and its Flight Termination System charges.

Based on timelines from Ship 40, 41, and so far 42, Ship 43 will be ready for static fire in mid-December and possibly ready for transport to Kennedy Space Center in early to mid-January.

Booster 23 completed cryo-proof testing on Oct. 15 and is slated to be ready for static fire testing in late November. Unlike ships, SpaceX can test Booster 23 on LC-39A, which will also help activate the pad systems.
